> Base: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40811

## Motivation

Quark-quantized Kimi-K3 on ROCm spends extra decode time on its weight layouts. It runs MXFP4 dense linears in fp4 (which costs accuracy), keeps the KDA input projection as separate linears, and leaves the shared experts outside the fused MoE front. It also runs the MLA absorb in bf16. This PR fixes each of these at load time.

## Modifications

- Decode MXFP4 dense-linear weights to bf16 at load, and let `SGLANG_ROCM_QUARK_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACT` choose bf16 or fp4 activations.
- Merge the per-channel FP8 KDA input projections into one FP8 linear that reuses the checkpoint scales.
- Register `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND` in `Envs` and read it through `envs` on the KDA decode path.
- Rename the FlyDSL KDA decode to the names in ROCm/aiter#6026: module `kda_decode`, entry points `flydsl_kda_decode`, `flydsl_kda_decode_with_f_b`, and `is_flydsl_kda_decode_supported`, kernel builders `kda_decode_gfx950` and `kda_decode_fused_projection_gfx950`. The AITER source now loads from `aiter.ops.flydsl.kda_decode`.
- Densify the MXFP4 shared experts so they join the fused MoE front.
- Requantize `kv_b` to per-tensor FP8 so the MLA absorb runs the AITER a8w8 batched GEMM.

| New env flag | Default |
|---|---|
| `SGLANG_ROCM_QUARK_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACT` | `bf16` |
| `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_QUARK_SHARED_FULL_FRONT` | on |
| `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_MLA_ABSORB_FP8` | on |

Shared (non-K3) files: `quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py`, `kda_fused_decode_aiter_hip.py`, `environ.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions:

| Base | This PR |
|---:|---:|
| 0.939 | **0.951** |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X, TP8, `Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`, random 8192 in / 1024 out, AITER `a9a702700`. Base and PR ran back to back on the same machine with the Kimi-K3 8k/1k recipe, which differs from the cookbook MI355X recipe: TP8 without DCP8, and `--disable-radix-cache`.

| Conc | TPOT (ms) base | TPOT (ms) PR | Δ | TTFT (ms) base | TTFT (ms) PR | Δ | Throughput (tok/s/GPU) base | Throughput (tok/s/GPU) PR | Δ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 19.05 | 14.95 | -21.5% | 803 | 825 | +2.7% | 113.5 | 142.9 | +25.9% |
| 4 | 20.72 | 16.53 | -20.2% | 1405 | 1399 | -0.4% | 204.3 | 251.6 | +23.2% |
| 8 | 23.32 | 19.28 | -17.3% | 2181 | 2221 | +1.8% | 354.6 | 420.2 | +18.5% |
| 16 | 28.51 | 24.26 | -14.9% | 3746 | 3854 | +2.9% | 560.4 | 641.8 | +14.5% |
| 32 | 36.52 | 32.66 | -10.6% | 6854 | 7107 | +3.7% | 837.6 | 914.0 | +9.1% |
| 64 | 51.39 | 47.91 | -6.8% | 13062 | 13586 | +4.0% | 1123.0 | 1177.5 | +4.9% |

Decode is faster at every concurrency, most at low concurrency: TPOT is 21.5% lower at c2 and 6.8% lower at c64. TTFT stays within 4% of the base.

Tests (MI355X): `test_quark_utils.py` (20), `test_kimi_k3_rocm_quant.py` (12), `test_kda_decode.py` (16), all passing.

### Storing shared experts in BF16

- Shared experts always run in BF16 in our recipe, so storing them as MXFP4 only adds a quantize-then-dequantize step at load.
- BF16 storage would remove that step. The `SGLANG_ROCM_QUARK_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACT` flag would then not be needed for these layers.
- Tradeoff: the checkpoint gets larger and uses more memory. Shared experts and layer-0 are a small part of total weights, so I expect the cost to be small.
- I'd keep the load-time dequantization path so existing MXFP4 checkpoints still work.

### Why the env var exists (internal harness)

- Harness: `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`, 5-shot, 512 tokens.
- Dense linears with BF16 activations: 94.7%.
- Dense linears with FP4 activations: 90.8%.
- This ~4-point gap is why we added `SGLANG_ROCM_QUARK_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACT=bf16`. The default is `bf16`.

### HF page test (separate harness, not comparable to the numbers above)

- Published vLLM: 96.36%.
- Our SGLang implementation: 96.3609% (1271/1319).
- The full SGLang recipe matches the published score.

### vLLM vs SGLang implementation

- vLLM uses the generic Quark / `FusedMoEFactory` path.
  - Routed experts are A16W4 by default, and A4W4 with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=1`.
- SGLang uses K3-specific post-load transforms and the AITER MXMoE runner.
  - Transforms include merged KDA projections, MLA absorb, MoE layouts, and selected MXFP4 dequantization.
  - It also uses FP8 KV cache and INT4 quick-reduce.

### Why A4W4 for routed experts

- Routed experts dominate compute and weight traffic, so FP4 activations help most here.
- A4W4 keeps both operands in MXFP4, and the AITER MXMoE path quantizes BF16 input inline, so it needs no separate A16W4 path.
- It matches vLLM's A4W4 mode and keeps the HF accuracy.

### Discussion

- Routed experts: A4W4.
- Shared experts and layer-0 dense: BF16.

Please let us know if you have other ideas.

> Base: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40811

## Motivation

Quark-quantized Kimi-K3 on ROCm spends extra decode time on its weight layouts. It runs MXFP4 dense linears in fp4 (which costs accuracy), keeps the KDA input projection as separate linears, and leaves the shared experts outside the fused MoE front. It also runs the MLA absorb in bf16. This PR fixes each of these at load time.

## Modifications

- Decode MXFP4 dense-linear weights to bf16 at load, and let `SGLANG_ROCM_QUARK_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACT` choose bf16 or fp4 activations.
- Merge the per-channel FP8 KDA input projections into one FP8 linear that reuses the checkpoint scales.
- Register `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND` in `Envs` and read it through `envs` on the KDA decode path.
- Rename the FlyDSL KDA decode to the names in ROCm/aiter#6026: module `kda_decode`, entry points `flydsl_kda_decode`, `flydsl_kda_decode_with_f_b`, and `is_flydsl_kda_decode_supported`, kernel builders `kda_decode_gfx950` and `kda_decode_fused_projection_gfx950`. - Densify the MXFP4 shared experts so they join the fused MoE front.

### Storing shared experts in BF16

- Shared experts always run in BF16 in our recipe, so storing them as MXFP4 only adds a quantize-then-dequantize step at load.
- BF16 storage would remove that step. The `SGLANG_ROCM_QUARK_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACT` flag would then not be needed for these layers.
- Tradeoff: the checkpoint gets larger and uses more memory. Shared experts and layer-0 are a small part of total weights, so I expect the cost to be small.
- I'd keep the load-time dequantization path so existing MXFP4 checkpoints still work.

### Why the env var exists (internal harness)

- Harness: `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`, 5-shot, 512 tokens.

- Dense linears with FP4 activations: 90.8%.

### vLLM vs SGLang implementation

- vLLM uses the generic Quark / `FusedMoEFactory` path.
  - Routed experts are A16W4 by default, and A4W4 with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=1`.
- SGLang uses K3-specific post-load transforms and the AITER MXMoE runner.
  - Transforms include merged KDA projections, MLA absorb, MoE layouts, and selected MXFP4 dequantization.
  - It also uses FP8 KV cache and INT4 quick-reduce.

### Why A4W4 for routed experts

- Routed experts dominate compute and weight traffic, so FP4 activations help most here.
- A4W4 keeps both operands in MXFP4, and the AITER MXMoE path quantizes BF16 input inline, so it needs no separate A16W4 path.
- It matches vLLM's A4W4 mode and keeps the HF accuracy.

- Routed experts: A4W4.
